question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: TYPE GRAMMAR. The type text is parsed completely before the value is looked at; any failure throws, whatever the value. The text must be exactly one TYPE, where TYPE is one ALT or two or more ALTs joined by "|" (a union, in written order), and ALT is one of: a scalar name from TABLE NODES (text bytes bool none i64 u64 f64 json); "tuple[" TYPE ("," TYPE)* "]" (one or more items); "list[" TYPE "]" (exactly one); "map[" TYPE "," TYPE "]" (exactly two); "record[" FIELD ("," FIELD)* "]" with FIELD = NAME ":" TYPE (one or more fields, names distinct). A NAME is a letter or "_" followed by letters, digits or "_" (ASCII only), and a word is always read greedily, so "textx" is an unknown name. Space, tab, carriage return and line feed may appear between ANY two tokens (a keyword and its "[" included) and at both ends — no other character is whitespace. Names are case-sensitive. So "text|", "text || none", "list[]", "record[]", "map[text]", "list[f64, text]", "record[text]", "record[0: none]" and "text none" all throw, while " record [ a : list [ f64 ] ] " parses. Composite types (tuple, list, map, record) nest at most MAX_DEPTH deep: a composite with MAX_DEPTH composites around it throws (16 nested lists around text parse, 17 throw); siblings do not add up (a tuple of two 15-deep lists is 16 deep).

UNREACHABLE ALTERNATIVES. A union (at any depth) throws the parse when a later alternative is COVERED by any earlier one of the same union. COVERS(a, b) — earlier a, later b — holds exactly when ANY of these holds: (a) SAME: a and b are the same type, where a union compares as the SET of its alternatives and a record as the SET of its named fields (orders immaterial; names and field types count), every other composite position by position; (b) a is json and b is JSON-REACHED: none, bool, f64, text or json; a list of a JSON-REACHED item; a tuple whose items are all JSON-REACHED; a map whose key type is exactly the scalar text (not a union holding it) and whose value type is JSON-REACHED; a record whose field types are all JSON-REACHED; a union of JSON-REACHED alternatives; (c) STRUCTURAL: both lists and COVERS(item, item); both tuples of the same length and COVERS item by item; both maps and COVERS on the key types and on the value types; both records and EVERY field of a has a field of the same name in b that it COVERS (b may have more fields, a may not); (d) b is a union and a COVERS every alternative of b; or a is a union and some alternative of a COVERS b. Nothing else counts (a record never covers a map, a list never a tuple, json never bytes, i64 or u64). So "none | none", "json | none", "json | tuple[text]", "json | record[a: text]", "list[json] | list[text]", "list[text | json] | list[json]", "map[text, json] | map[text, text]" and "record[a: text] | record[a: text, b: none]" throw, while "none | json", "json | i64", "json | tuple[i64]", "json | map[json, f64]", "json | map[text | none, f64]", "list[text] | list[text | none]", "tuple[json, json] | tuple[text]", "record[a: text, b: none] | record[a: text]" and "tuple[text, none] | tuple[none, text]" parse. NOTE coverage is decided on types alone: an alternative R2 refuses may still be the only one that accepts some value (the absent value under none, a record's unread members) — the parse refuses it all the same (FIDELITY package).

THROW OBSERVATIONS. At every TYPED position — the top, each union alternative, each tuple or list item, each map key and value, each record field, and the top of a json position — the value is first tested, before the type is consulted: a map with EXACTLY ONE member, named "__throw" or "__threw", whose value is text encodes as the node t throw with msg = that text. A second member of any kind makes it an ordinary map ({"__throw": "x", "a": 1} is a map, and {"__t": "num", "v": "5", "__throw": "x"} is the num tag of R5); a non-text marker value is an ordinary member. Only a map is ever a throw observation (never a list), and an ESCAPED map (R5) never is. Inside json content (below the top of a json position) such maps are ordinary maps.

ABSENT. The absent value arises from a record field the value lacks (R8) or an undef tag (R5). It encodes as t none where the type is none or a union with a none alternative, and throws everywhere else — json included.

LEGACY TAGS. After R3, a map holding a text member "__t" (and not ESCAPED) is a v0.4 codec tag and is replaced by the value it stands for before the type is applied — at every typed position, and at every node inside json content: num: member v must be text: "NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity" or "-0" give those numbers; otherwise v must spell a json number literal (optional "-", then "0" or a digit 1-9 and more digits, optional "." and one or more digits, optional "e" or "E", optional sign, one or more digits) and gives its nearest double. The literal is a VALUE, not a spelling: "1E3", "1000.0" and "1000" all give 1000. It throws when that double is infinite ("1e999", "-1e999"); when it is zero of either sign while the MANTISSA (the literal before any "e" or "E") holds a digit 1-9 — an underflow: "1e-400", "-1e-400", "2e-324", "0.1e-323", while "3e-324" gives the least subnormal; and when it is -0 ("-0.0", "-0e5"). So a zero is accepted only from an unsigned literal whose mantissa digits are all 0 ("0", "0e5", "0.000"). Anything else throws ("", "00", "+1", ".5", a non-text v). bigint: v must be text spelling a decimal integer in its one canonical form ("0", or an optional "-" then a digit 1-9 and more digits — so "-0" and "007" throw); it gives that exact integer (an integer kind that is not a number, R6); anything else throws. undef: the absent value (R4). obj (the escape of a user map): member v must be a map — none, a missing v, a list, text, a number or a bool throws. The result is a NEW map, ESCAPED, holding v's entries. ESCAPED means the new map's own members "__t", "__throw" and "__threw" are DATA at that node wherever it is then encoded (a union retries alternatives on the same escaped map); its entry VALUES are ordinary, so R3 and R5 apply to them. Any other tag name throws. Members of a tag map beyond those named are ignored ({__t: "num", v: "5", x: 1} gives 5).
SCALARS AND CONTAINERS encode by TABLE NODES. A value outside a row's accept set throws (inside a union: the next alternative is tried).
none | none or the absent value | t none
bool | a bool | t bool, v = the bool
text | well-formed text | t text, v = the text, cu = "utf8"
f64 | any number | t f64, v = RENDER(x), bits = BITS(x)
i64 | an integral number or an integer, within -2^63 .. 2^63-1 | t i64, v = the exact value in decimal ("-" for negatives, no leading zeros; -0 gives "0")
u64 | an integral number or an integer, within 0 .. 2^64-1 | t u64, v as for i64
bytes | a byte string | t bytes, v = "base64:" then the standard base64 alphabet with "=" padding (RFC 4648 section 4); none in json
json | see R10 | the json node tree
tuple[T1..Tn] | a list of exactly n items | t tuple, v = item i encoded under Ti
list[T] | any list | t list, v = each item encoded under T
map[K, V] | a map or a keyed collection (not a list) | t map, v = the entries as pairs [key encoded under K, value encoded under V], sorted by R9
record[...] | a map (not a list, not a keyed collection) | t record, v = one pair [field name as plain text, field encoded under its type] per field, in written order
union | see R7 | the first alternative's node

UNIONS. Tags are resolved once (R5) — a malformed tag at the union's own position throws the union before any alternative is tried — then the alternatives are tried in written order on that value and the FIRST that encodes it without throwing — anywhere inside it, R13 included — wins; when every alternative throws, the union throws. A throw anywhere inside a list, tuple, map, record or json content throws that whole container. So "i64 | f64" gives 1 as i64 and "f64 | i64" gives it as f64.

RECORD READS. A field reads the map's OWN entry of exactly that name (a key spelled __proto__ or constructor is an ordinary key), or the absent value when there is none. A map position takes the map's own entries; over a map the keys are always text, so a key type that rejects text (i64, none, …) throws on any non-empty map.

MAP ORDER — one order for every map, typed (map[K, V]) and json alike. Entries sort ascending by a sort key compared as sequences of 16-bit code units: a text key's sort key is the key text itself; any other key's is CANON of its encoded node (R11). Entries with equal sort keys keep their input order (reachable only through a host keyed collection).

JSON. A json position (after R3 at its top) encodes recursively, R5 applied at every node: none -> t none; bool; a number -> the f64 node; text -> the text node (well-formed); a list -> t list of its items' json nodes; a map -> t map whose pairs are [text node of the key, json node of the value], sorted by R9. Everything else throws: the absent value, an integer that is not a number, a byte string, a keyed collection, a list with a hole, a non-plain host object.

CANON. The canonical string of an encoded node: compact json text with map members sorted by key (16-bit code units), strings written as ESC inside double quotes, booleans as true / false, lists in order; an f64 node is reduced to its members bits and t, a throw node to t alone. So an i64 key reads {"t":"i64","v":"10"} (decimal text order: "10" before "9"), an f64 key {"bits":"…","t":"f64"}; against a text key the comparison is the raw text versus that string.
double quote | "\""
backslash | "\\"
any other code 0-31 | "\u00" then two lowercase hex digits
every other character | itself

RENDER(x) is the ECMA-262 Number::toString(x) radix-10 rendering (the fewest digits that round-trip and, among digit strings of that length, the one closest to x; exponent form below 1e-6 and from 1e21, written "1e+21", "1e-7", "1.5e-7"; integral values below 1e21 in full positional form, so 123456789012345680000), except -0 renders "-0"; NaN, Infinity and -Infinity render "NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity". BITS(x) is the IEEE-754 binary64 bit pattern as 16 lowercase hex digits, most significant first; every NaN gives "7ff8000000000000".

NESTING CAP. Values have depths: the whole value is depth 0 and each CHILD value is one deeper than its parent — a list or tuple item, a map key and a map value, a record field value (the absent value of a missing field included), and inside json content a list item and a map value. A union alternative, the json position and a legacy tag (R5) are the SAME value at the same depth; an escaped map's entry values (R5 obj) are its children. Encoding a value at depth greater than MAX_VALUE_DEPTH throws (inside a union: an ordinary alternative failure). So under "json" 100 nested lists around a scalar encode (the scalar sits at depth 100) and 101 throw; 100 nested lists around an EMPTY list encode; under "list[json] | none" and under 16 typed lists around json the same 101-deep value throws. Typed positions alone cannot reach the cap (types nest at most MAX_DEPTH, R1); it is met inside json content.
